one will be able to bring about all benefits and remain free from every fault.
Furthermore, regarding the syllable VA, the practitioner, relying on yoga,
understands the ritual procedures for performing activities; for the sake of benefiting sentient beings,
the Savior of the World within his own body is entirely like this.
The water of the mind is deep and full, pure white like snow or milk;
one should give rise to a resolute intention that issues forth from the entire body,
pervading all the pores, flowing forth with supreme purity.
From this, it flows inwardly in abundance, pervading the entire great earth;
with these waters of compassion, he beholds sentient beings suffering in the world.
All those who drink or use them, or even those whose bodies are touched by them, [are purified].
All are definitively certain to attain the realization of Bodhi.
Contemplating within meditative equipoise, all the *ra*-gateways radiate flames in a circular array;
they shine forth in total stillness, illuminating everywhere.
The light of the *yoginī* radiates outward, pervading all places.
To benefit the world according to their inclinations, the practitioner gives rise to supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*).
The syllable *raṃ* is at the upper body, and the syllable *vaṃ* is in the navel wheel.
Fire issues forth and rain falls, appearing simultaneously in response.
The extreme cold and suffering of the hells are eliminated by the syllable *ra*,
and the blazing heat is dispelled by the syllable *va*, because one abides in the power of the mantra-dharma.
The syllable RA constitutes the lower body, and the syllable HA is the insignia;
it swiftly accomplishes activities and rescues sentient beings from grave sins.
Abiding in Mahendra, it performs the rites of the water-dragons.
All gathering, removing, and so forth—let the mantra-practitioner have no doubt.
Wind pervades all places; it opens and destroys everything.
These various and diverse types each perform their manifold activities.
Within the form maṇḍala, perform the rites according to the dharma.
Contemplating and maintaining mindfulness with the mind, one attains purity of the sense faculty of the mind.
Lightly rising to practice walking meditation, one recites within and acquires the supernormal powers.
"Sitting in meditative repose, contemplate the syllable A; let the visualization rest upon the faculty of hearing.
If you maintain this recollection for a full month, you shall attain purity of hearing.
"Lord of Mysteries!"
Such are the phrases for the *manomaya-siddhi*, O Lord of Secrets!

Observe that these arise from various kinds of practices that have no form or color; by merely reciting them for the duration of a single thought-moment, they can produce all such seeds of virtuous karma.
Furthermore, Guhyakādhipati!

There is nothing that the Tathāgata does not accomplish. To all bodhisattvas practicing through the gateway of mantras, he appears as if reflected in a mirror; he accords with all places and accords with the heart of all mantras, remaining ever present before them, causing all sentient beings to attain joy. This is entirely due to the Tathāgata’s non-conceptual intention, which is free from all objective spheres.
And he spoke in verse:
"There is no time or place for its creation; Transcending both dharma and adharma, it bestows the words of siddhi; Thus is the arising of the mantra practice."
Therefore, the All-Knowing One, the fruit of the Tathāgata’s *siddhi*, is the most supreme and honored state; one should bring it to accomplishment.
At that time, Śrīvajra, with his wondrously blossoming eyes, [spoke].
Turning the Vajra-mudrā with his hands, he radiates light like shimmering flames;
its brilliance shines universally upon all Buddha-fields,
while a subtle and wondrous voice offers praise:
“The Sage, Sovereign of Dharma, has taught all mantra practices.
Since those practices cannot be apprehended, from where do mantras come?
And to what place do they go?”
"The Buddhas have spoken thus; there is no statement superior to this.
All phenomena converge herein, just as all rivers flow toward the ocean.
Having spoken these words, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:
“The sphere of the mind of the Mahāsattva is called the maṇḍala;
by thoroughly understanding the positions of the heart of all mantras, one attains the fruition of the result.
Whatever conceptualizations there may be, they all arise from the mind.”
Discriminating between white, yellow, and red—these arise from the mind.
When the mind is resolute and joyful, it is called the "inner locus.
When the mantra abides in this state, it can bestow vast fruits.
One should contemplate that lotus abode, with its eight petals and spreading filaments and anthers;
upon the flower pedestal is the gateway of the letter A, its garlands of flames exquisite and beautiful,
its radiance universally pervasive, illuminating all sentient beings.
Like a convergence of a thousand flashes of lightning, the Buddha sustains skillful forms and colors;
dwelling deeply within the perfect mirror, he manifests throughout all places.
Like the moon in clear water, he appears universally before the eyes of all sentient beings.
Knowing the nature of the mind to be thus, one attains the practice of the mantra.
Next, upon the crown of the head, at the junction where the channels meet,
one marks it with the great bindu of emptiness and contemplates the syllable *Aṃ*.
Exquisite, pure, and stainless, like rock crystal, the moon, or lightning,
he proclaims the tranquil Dharmakāya, the support of all things.
Through the siddhis of all mantras, he is able to manifest in various forms.
Attaining the liberation of celestial music, one reaches the state of the Tathāgata.
The syllable RA constitutes the visual faculty; its radiance is like that of a bright lamp.
With the neck slightly bent and the head bowed low, the tongue is held close to the palate.
By means of observing the locus of the mind, one should manifest meditative equipoise within the mind—
stainless, wondrously pure, and clear, with the circular mirror constantly appearing before one.
Such is the true mind, as proclaimed by the Buddhas of antiquity.
The illuminating mind is clearly realized, and all forms emit light.
The practitioner of mantras shall behold the Perfectly Awakened One, the Honored One among Two-legged Beings;
if he beholds him, he will achieve *siddhi*, the foremost and eternal essence.
From this point, one should contemplate and transform this syllable *ra*;
by placing the *ra* with the great empty bindu (*visarga*) in the position of the eyes,
one sees the phrase of universal emptiness and attains the state of the immortal.
If one desires vast wisdom, or wishes to attain the five supernormal powers,
a long-lived body as a youth, or the accomplishments of a vidyādhara and so forth,
yet the mantra practitioner has not attained them, it is because they have failed to practice in accordance with these instructions.
The wisdom generated by mantras is the most supreme and true knowledge;
it is the treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who save the world.
From this arise all the Perfectly Awakened Ones and the Bodhisattvas who save the world.
And all the śrāvakas and others, traveling to other regions throughout all buddha-fields, everywhere proclaim these words:
"Thus one attains unsurpassed wisdom; the Buddha’s wisdom is beyond compare."

Chapter Eight: The Practice of the Maṇḍala of the Revolving Wheel of Syllables At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana surveyed the entire great assembly; with eyes cultivated through great compassion, he beheld the realm of sentient beings and dwelt in the *amṛtarāja-samādhi*.
At that time, by virtue of this samādhi, the Buddha further spoke the vidyā-mantra of the Vidyārājñī of Unobstructed Power throughout the Three Times:
"Tadyathā | gagana-same | aprati-samae | sarva-tathāgata-samadhyanugate | gaganasame | varalokṣaṇe | svāhā. "O son of good family!"
By means of this consort’s non-dual realm of the Tathāgata’s body, he spoke these verses:
“Through the empowerment of the Buddha, The Bodhisattva of great renown,
Is unimpeded regarding all phenomena, And is able to extinguish all suffering.”

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana, recollecting that all Buddhas are primordially unborn, empowered himself and the Holder of the Vajra, and addressed the foremost Vajradharas, such as Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"O sons of good family!
“Listen attentively to the chapter on the practice of the Maṇḍala of the Revolving Syllable Wheel.
Bodhisattvas who practice through the gateway of mantras are able to perform the Buddha-work by universally manifesting their bodies.
At that time, the Vajradhara descended, turning away from his vajra-lotus seat, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, and praised him, saying:
"Homage to the bodhicitta! Homage to the arousal of bodhicitta!
I prostrate to the essence of the practices, the stages, the perfections, and so forth."
"I respectfully pay homage to those who first performed these deeds, and take refuge in those who have realized emptiness.
Having thus offered praise, the Lord of Secrets addressed the Buddha, saying:

"I pray that the Dharma King, out of compassion, will protect and mind us and expound this, for the benefit of sentient beings and so that the cultivation of mantras may be brought to perfection as taught."
When he had spoken thus, the World-Honored One Vairocana addressed the Vajradhara Lord of Mysteries, saying:
"I am the primordial of all, named the Support of the World;
my teaching of the Dharma is peerless, fundamentally quiescent and unsurpassed."
Then, as the Buddha spoke this verse, he performed such an empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*).

By virtue of that empowerment, the Vajradharas and all the Bodhisattvas were able to see the seat of the supreme vow, the Bodhi of the Buddha; the World-Honored One appeared like space, free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*), non-dual in its conduct, and characterized by yoga.

When this karma ripened, at that very moment, these syllables appeared upon all the limbs of the World-Honored One’s body. In all mundane and supramundane states, and in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, those who diligently cultivate contemplation and achieve *siddhi* shall all have the same lifespan, the same seed-syllable, the same basis, and the same Savior.
"Namo samantabuddhānām. Ā. 'O son of good family!
This syllable Ā is empowered by all Tathāgatas.'"

Bodhisattvas who practice the bodhisattva path through the gateway of mantras are able to perform the buddha-work by universally manifesting their form bodies, turning all dharmas within the gateway of the letter A.
Therefore, O Lord of Secrets!

Bodhisattvas who practice the bodhisattva path through the gateway of mantras—whether they wish to see the Buddha, to make offerings, to realize the arousal of the bodhicitta, to assemble together with other bodhisattvas, to benefit sentient beings, to seek siddhi, or to seek omniscience—should diligently cultivate this heart of all Buddhas.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana further definitively expounded the inconceivable dharmas of the samādhi, supernormal powers, and mantra-practices for the arrangement of the positions of the holy deities within the King of Maṇḍalas Born from the Matrix of Great Compassion.

That Ācārya first abides in the gateway of all-knowledge, the letter A; holding the sūtra, he prostrates to all Buddhas, extends it toward the east, rotates it to the south and then to the west, and finally completes the circuit in the north.

Next, one becomes Vajrasattva and empowers oneself with the Vajra-holding empowerment; either by means of that mudrā or by means of the syllable *Vaṃ*, one enters into the inner heart and places [the deity] within the maṇḍala.
Thus, in this second maṇḍala as well, because one’s own body is empowered by primordial quiescence, there are the forms of non-dual yoga, the Tathāgata, and emptiness.
Next, having relinquished the two portions of the path he had traversed, he leaves behind the three realms of the noble ones and devas, abides in the stage of the Tathāgata,
and extends the sūtra toward the east, revolving it in a complete circle.
The remaining two maṇḍalas should likewise perform all ritual activities through this same expedient means.
Furthermore, one should empower oneself with Mahāvairocana, contemplate the vast dharmadhātu, and arrange the various colors.
"The mantra practitioner should prioritize purity.
He spoke a verse, saying:
"By means of this pure Dharma-realm, purify all sentient beings."
The self-nature is like the Tathāgata, Far removed from all faults.
Contemplate it thus: Visualize the syllable-gateway *ra*, Tranquil, with a garland of blazing flames, The color of a pure moon or a conch shell.
Second, one should arrange the color red; the practitioner should maintain it in mind and contemplate the syllable as brilliantly illuminating.
It is the primordial non-existence, the great bindu, radiant like the glow of the rising sun—the most supreme, which nothing can destroy.
The third mantra practitioner next arrays the yellow color;
with the mind fixed on the gateway of the syllable KA, one should follow the instructions of the Dharma.
His physical form is like pure gold, truly able to subdue all poisons.
Light pervades all, its golden hue like that of the Muni.
Next, one should spread the blue color; having transcended birth and death, one contemplates the gateway of the syllable Ma, the seat of great tranquility and bodhi.
The body’s color is like a rainbow, removing all fears;
finally, it is draped in black, its hues most profound and wondrous.
Contemplating the gateway of the syllable HA, a circular light is produced everywhere.
"Like the fierce flames at the end of an eon, with a jeweled crown and raised hand-mudrā,
he can terrify all evils and subdue the armies of all Māras.
At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana arose from samādhi and dwelt in the immeasurable supreme concentration.
Within meditative absorption, the Buddha manifested the Vidyārājñī of Pervasive Invincibility, who arises from the realm of all Tathāgatas.
Her mantra is as follows:

*Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo viśva-mukhebhyaḥ | asa me | prame | ajare | gaganasamale | sarvatrānugate | svāhā.* Next, having prepared the colors and prostrated to the World-Honored One and the Prajñāpāramitā, one should recite this Vidyārājñī eight times.
Rising from his seat, he circumambulates the maṇḍala and enters into his inner mind, contemplating all disciples with the power of great loving-kindness and great compassion.

The ācārya further empowers himself as Karma-Vajrasattva; having performed the *vajradvāra* and the *varada-vajra*, he should then draw the Great Maṇḍala born from the Matrix of Great Compassion (*Mahākaruṇāgarbhodbhava*).

With composure, one should visualize oneself as the World-Honored One Vairocana within the inner mind: seated upon a white lotus, with a topknot of hair upon his head, wearing a *pata* as a lower garment and draped in fine gauze silk; his body is golden in color and encircled by a wreath of flames;
or else, one may employ the Tathāgata-Uṣṇīṣa Mudrā, or the syllable-gate known as the letter *A*.
All Buddhas of the eastern direction, by means of the letter-gateway A and the great dot of emptiness;
and for the Mother of all Tathāgatas, Ākāśanetra, in the Īśāna direction, one should write the letter GA.
In the direction of Agni (the southeast), all the bodhisattvas should be depicted; one should either paint a cintāmaṇi jewel or place the syllable KA there.

In the direction of the yakṣas (the northeast), there is Avalokiteśvara with the lotus mudrā, along with his retinue of bodhisattvas who are in their last birth before Buddhahood; or one may depict the syllable SA.
In the direction of Yama, one should skip three parts and place the Vajra Wisdom Seal (Vajrajñānamudrā), as well as the Vajra Secret Lord (Vajraguhyapati) together with his retinue;
or one may write the syllable *vaḥ*. Then, skipping another three parts, one should draw the seals of all the Vajradharas;
or one may write the words and phrases, namely the syllable *hūṃ*.

Next, in the direction of Nairṛti, beneath the Tathāgata Vairocana, one should depict the Honored One Acala seated upon a stone, holding a noose and a wisdom-sword in his hands, with a wreath of flames encircling him as if to ward off obstructors; or one may place his mudrā there, or write the syllables, namely the syllable *haṃ*.

In the direction of the Wind Deity, the Honored One Trailokyavijaya, the Destroyer of Great Obstacles, has flames above him; his great power and wrath are like those of Yama. His form is black, most terrifying among all that is fearsome, and he brandishes a vajra with his hand.
Alternatively, one may form that mudrā or write the syllable and phrase, namely the long-voweled letter *Ha*.
Next, one should draw the four great protectors in the four directions.

In the direction of Śakra, one draws the Fearless Binding Protector (*Abhayabandhana*), who is golden in color and wears white robes, with a face manifesting a slight wrathful expression, holding a *daṇḍa* or forming that mudrā, or else placing the syllable and phrase, namely the letter *Va*.
In the yakṣa direction is the one named Destroyer of All Fears and Protector, white in color and wearing white garments, holding a khaḍga sword with radiating flames; he is able to destroy all fears.
Alternatively, his mudrā may be depicted, or the syllable *va* may be placed there.

In the direction of the Dragon (the north), there is the one named Difficult-to-Subdue Protector, who is also the color of an *aśoka* flower, wears crimson robes, has a smiling countenance, and gazes upon the entire assembly from within a blaze of light;
alternatively, one may place his seal or the syllable *sa*, known as the "Seeking" (*sō*) syllable.

In the direction of Yama is the one named Vajrāparājita-kṣepa-rakṣaka (Vajra Invincible Binding Protector). He is black in color and wears dark robes; his form is that of Bhīḍṛcī, with a wavy mark between his eyebrows and a hair-crown upon his head. His own majestic light illuminates the realms of sentient beings, and he holds a *daṇḍa* (staff), capable of destroying those who create great obstacles.
Alternatively, one may perform his mudrā or place the syllable *kṣam*, together with all his retinues and messengers, seated upon white lotus flowers.

Once the mantra practitioner has thus arranged [the mandala], he should next go outside and, in the second section, draw Śākyamuni, the King of Munis of the Śākya clan, clad in the saṃghāṭī robe and possessing the thirty-two marks of a Great Teacher, expounding the most supreme teaching for the sake of bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings;
or [he may depict him] with the mudrās of the saṃghāṭī and the alms bowl, or by means of syllables, namely the letter *ba*.

Next, within the outer maṇḍala, one should empower oneself with the nature of the *dharmadhātu*, generate the bodhicitta, relinquish the three stages of existence, and perform three prostrations while mentally recollecting the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana, adjusting the colors as previously described.

In the third section, in the direction of Śakra, one should fashion the form of the Vajrakumāra of Bestowing Boons (*Varada-vajrakumāra*). He holds a blue lotus in his *samādhi* hand, upon which rests a vajra of wisdom (*prajñā-vajra*). He adorns himself with various necklaces and ornaments; he wears a lower garment of exquisite, fine silk, and for his upper garment, he uses cloth that is extremely light and delicate.
His body is the color of *uragasāra* gold, and his head has five topknots. Alternatively, one may place a secret seal (*mudrā*) or seed-syllables there.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ. To his right is the youth Jālinīprabha, whose every limb is perfectly complete; his Samādhi hand holds a jeweled net, and his Wisdom hand holds a hook.
Alternatively, one may place his mudrā there, or write the syllable, namely the letter *ra*.
In the direction of Yama, one should depict the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, with golden hair and a crown, holding a wish-fulfilling jewel;
or else one may draw his mudrā, or place the syllable and phrase known as the long-sounding syllable "Aḥ."
In the yakṣa direction is Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, whose color is like that of a pāṇḍuraka flower; he holds a lotus in his hand and is adorned with various necklaces and ornaments;
alternatively, his seal may be placed there, or the syllable *i* may be inscribed.

In the direction of the Dragon (North), there is Ākāśagarbha, white in color and clad in white garments, his body emitting flames of light and adorned with various necklaces; he holds a sword (khaḍga) in his hand;
alternatively, one may place his seal or the syllable "I" with a long vowel.
“The mantra practitioner, seated in meditative repose, dwells securely within the dharmadhātu;
realizing ‘I am the very nature of the dharmadhātu,’ he abides in the bodhicitta.
Facing the direction of Śakra, he binds the seal of Vajraprajñā.”
Next, perform the vajra-activities and diligently cultivate offerings.
Manifesting the Buddhas who save the world, [employ] the samaya-mudrās and so forth;
while contemplating all directions and locations, recite the mantra three times.
According to the ritual, summon the disciples and purify them as they face the maṇḍala;
bestow upon them the three refuges and establish them in the supreme bodhicitta.
For the sake of all disciples, one should bind the mudrā of the nature of the dharmadhātu.
Next, bind the Dharma-wheel mudrā and with single-mindedness identify yourself with its essence.
Cover the face with silk cloth and arouse a heart of compassion;
cause the hands to become "not empty," so that bodhi may be perfected.
Whispering into his ear, one should inform him of the unsurpassed, perfectly equal precepts;
next, one should bind for him the seal of the perfectly equal samādhi.
Bestowing upon him a blossoming flower, one causes him to generate the aspiration for enlightenment (bodhicitta).
"Wherever you go, teach the students. Make this solemn vow: 'All should be transmitted [to others]'—O Virtuous Vajradhara."
Again, he addressed the Blessed One:
"I pray only that the Supreme among Benevolent Ones will expound the empowerment dharma.
At that time, the Bhagavān, abiding in the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), [responded].
Then he addressed Vajrapāṇi:
“Listen with a single-minded focus as I proclaim the teachings on all phenomena, which are held by the supreme sovereign.
The Master, through the nature of the Tathāgata, empowers his own body.”
Alternatively, using the secret mudrā, one should next summon the disciples and cause them to abide within the nature of the dharmadhātu,
amidst the Great Lotus King. With the precious vases empowered by the four great bodhisattvas,
Forming the mudrā of the arising of the branches of enlightenment, one should use it to consecrate the crown of the head.
Within the topknot, one should bestow the letter-gateway of the Great Emptiness (Aṃ);
at the heart, one places the phrase of non-arising; and upon the chest, one displays the stainless syllable (Vam).
"Or all [beings] with the letter A, their topknots radiating golden light,
dwelling upon white lotus pedestals, are identical to you, O Benevolent One.
*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Empowerment of the Buddha’s Miraculous Transformations*, Scroll Three.
The Mahāvairocana-abhisambodhi-vikurvaṇādhiṣṭhāna-sūtra,
Scroll Four.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Yi-xing. Chapter Nine: The Secret Mudrās. At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana surveyed the entire great assembly and addressed the Vajradhara Lord of Mysteries, saying: “Lord of Mysteries!

Possessing ornaments identical to those of the Tathāgata and bearing the insignia of the orientation toward the Dharmadhātu, the Bodhisattva adorns his body thereby; thus, while dwelling within saṃsāra and traversing the various realms of existence, he marks himself with this great banner of bodhi at the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas. Devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others revere him, circumambulate him, and proceed according to his instructions.
"Listen now attentively and reflect upon this well; I shall expound it.
Having spoken thus, Vajrapāṇi said to him, "World-Honored One!"
Now is precisely the time,
World-Honored One!
Now is precisely the time!
At that time, the Bhagavān immediately entered the samādhi called "The Power of Harmlessness toward the Body.
Abiding in this concentration, he spoke the mantra of the Vidyārājñī of the Unsurpassed Power of All-Pervading Non-Obstruction, which is the entry into the Samaya of all Tathāgatas:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Asame tṛsame samaye svāhā.* "O Lord of Secrets!..."
In this way, the consort manifests the ground of all Tathāgatas; she does not transcend the perfection of the ground that fulfills the realm of the path of the three dharmas.

This is the form of the secret mudrā: one should join the hands of concentration and wisdom in the hollow-palms gesture, and then establish it by joining the two space-wheels of concentration and wisdom together.
The verse says:
"All these Buddhas, the great seal that rescues the world,
abide within this seal of the samaya of perfect awakening."
"Furthermore, form fists with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, place the space-wheel (thumb) within the palms, and extend the wind-wheel (index finger); this is the Seal of the Pure Dharma-realm."

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ dharmadhātu-svabhāvātmako 'ham. Furthermore, with the hands of concentration and wisdom, all five fingers are equalized; they are interlaced and hooked with one another, while the two thumbs (the space-fingers) are both turned toward each other at their tips.
The verse says:
"This is called the Supreme Vow, the Auspicious Seal of the Wheel of Dharma;
all those who are Refuges for the World and Saviors of the World turn this very wheel."
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vajratma kūṃ*.

Then, extending the hands of concentration and wisdom, perform the *namaskāra-añjali* (palms joined in homage); interlace the *vāyu-maṇḍalas* (ring fingers) and place the two *ākāśa-maṇḍalas* (thumbs) upon them, forming the shape of a sword (*khaḍga*).
The verse says:
"This seal of the Great Wisdom Sword was spoken by all Buddhas;
it can sever all views, namely the innate view of a self-body."
The mantra is as follows:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | mahākhaḍgavirāja dharmasandarśaka sāhasika satkāyanirghātana tathāgatadhimuktiniḥpattihetuka virāgadharmaniḥpatti hūṃ*. Furthermore, with the hands of concentration and wisdom, form the hollow-palms gesture (*añjali*), bend the two wind-wheels (index fingers), and interlace the two space-wheels (thumbs) so that the shape resembles a conch shell (*śaṅkha*).
The verse says:
"This is named the Supreme Vow, the Auspicious Dharma Conch Seal;
the Buddhas, Teachers of the World, and the Bodhisattvas, Saviors of the World."
"All teach the stainless Dharma, leading to the tranquility of Nirvāṇa.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āḥ*.

Then, with the hands of concentration and wisdom joined together, extend and disperse them like a *kaṅka* bird; hold the two earth-wheels and the two space-wheels together, causing the fire-wheel and the wind-wheel to merge.
The verse says:
"May the auspicious lotus be fulfilled; the Buddhas, saviors of the world, awaken upon the indestructible vajra-seat, and are thus called Buddhas."
"Bodhi and the sons of the Buddha are all born from this.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āḥ*.
Then, with the hands of concentration and wisdom, form fists with the five fingers pointing outward and extend the fire-wheel (the middle finger).
Extend the two wind-wheels (index fingers) and bend them into the shape of hooks, holding them at the sides.
The space-wheel (thumbs) and earth-wheel (little fingers) are aligned and extended upward, while the water-wheels (middle fingers) are joined together like a *vajra*.
The verse says:
"The Great Wisdom Seal of the Vajra can destroy the city of ignorance;
it awakens those who sleep, and neither gods nor humans can destroy it."
The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ hūṃ*.
Then, with the hands of concentration and wisdom, form fists by turning the five fingers inward and extend the fire-fingers (*teja-aṅguli*).
Place the two wind-mudrās (index fingers) alongside and bend the two space-mudrās (thumbs) together.
The verse says:
"This mudrā is the Mahāmudrā, Known as the Tathāgata-uṣṇīṣa."
"Having just now formed [the mudrā], one is identical to the World-Honored One. The mantra is:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ hūṃ hūṃ. Again, form a fist with the wisdom hand and place it between the eyebrows.
The verse says:
"This is named the Uṣṇīṣa-kośa, the Seal of the Buddha’s Constant Fulfillment of Vows;
by merely forming it, one immediately becomes equal to the Most Excellent among Men."

The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām āḥ haṃ jaḥ*. Sitting upon the yoga-seat, in accordance with the practice of holding the alms-bowl, place both the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā together at the level of the navel; this is called the Great Alms-Bowl Seal of Śākyamuni.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ bhaḥ. Furthermore, with the hand of wisdom, turn it upward and form the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*).
The verse says:
"One who can bestow fearlessness upon all classes of sentient beings—
if they bind this great seal, they are called 'Bestower of Fearlessness'."
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | sarvathā | īne īne | peyanaśane | svāhā. Next, with the wisdom hand, extend it downward and form the mudrā of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*).
The verse says:
"This Seal of Granting Wishes was taught by the Refuge of the World;
as soon as it is bound, all Buddhas fulfill one's wishes."

The mantra is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vārāṇavajratmakāya svāhā*. Furthermore, form a fist with the wisdom hand (*prajñāhasta*), extend the wind-wheel (*vāyutattva*), and abide in meditative equipoise (*samādhi*) in the form of Bhṛkuṭī.
The verse says:
"By means of this great seal, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Saviors, terrify all obstructors;
one accomplishes siddhi according to one's wish."
"By binding this mudrā, the hosts of the great Māra armies and all other obstructors will scatter in flight without hindrance.
The mantra is as follows:

“Namo samantabuddhānāṃ | mahāmāravati | daśavalopave | mahāmataryābhyudgate | svāhā. Furthermore, form a fist with the wisdom hand, extend the fire-wheel (middle finger) and water-wheel (ring finger), and place the space-wheel (thumb) beneath them.
The verse says:
"This is called the eye of all Buddhas, The eye born of compassion, the refuge of the world.
If one visualizes it as being placed within the field of vision, The wise person attains the Buddha-eye."
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | gaganavaralocanā-karuṇā-mana-stathāgata-cakṣuḥ svāhā. Furthermore, with the hands in the mudrā of concentration, form fists with the five wheels [fingers] turned inward, extend the wind-wheel [index fingers], and join them together in a circular bend.
The verse says:
"This seal of the supreme wish-fulfilling lasso destroys all evildoers;
when bound by the mantra-practitioner, it can fetter all that is unwholesome."
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | He he mahāpūjā-prasādanīya | sattvadhātu-vimokṣaka | tathāgatādhiṣṭhāniteśvara | svāhā. Furthermore, joining the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā together to form a fist, extend the hand of Prajñā, and bend the third joint of the wind-wheel (the ring finger) so that it resembles a ring.
The verse says:
"This is called the Hook Seal; by it, all the Buddhas, the saviors of the world, who abide on the ten stages, are summoned and gathered."
"Those with the great mind of Bodhi, as well as sentient beings of evil intent.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Āḥ sarvatrāpratihatatejastathāgataghoṣa bodhicittotpādaka svāhā. This same hook-seal (aṅkuśa-mudrā), with the fire-wheel (the middle finger) extended and slightly bent, is called the Tathāgata-heart seal.
The mantra for this is:
“Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ raṅgudbhava svāhā. Furthermore, by extending the water-wheel (ring finger) of this mudrā and holding it upright, it is called the Tathāgata Navel Mudrā.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, amṛtodvave, svāhā. Then, with this same mudrā, extend the water-wheel (ring finger) straight out and keep the others upright; this is called the Tathāgata Waist Mudrā.

The mantra for this is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgatasaṃbhava svāhā. Furthermore, with the hands of concentration and wisdom joined in the hollow-palms gesture (*śūnyagarbha-muṣṭi*), bend the two *vāyu* fingers (the index fingers) inward; do the same for the two *toya* fingers (the middle fingers). Slightly bend the two *pṛthivī* fingers (the ring fingers) and extend the two *tejas* fingers (the little fingers). This is the Tathāgata-garbha mudrā.
The mantra for this is:
"Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo raṃ raṃ hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Then, with this same mudrā, one disperses the water-wheels and places them facing upward; this is called the Great Boundary Mudrā (Mahā-sīmā-mudrā).

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, līlupurvikule svāhā. Then, using this same mudrā, hooking and joining the two fire-wheels (the thumbs) while extending the wind-wheels (the index fingers), it is called the Great Protection Mudrā of Intolerance.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo viśvamukhebhyaḥ | sarvavidyādharebhyaḥ | viśvamukhebhyaḥ | svāhā | haṃ khaṃ | rakṣa mahāmāle | sarvatathāgatadharmatāniṣpattaye | hūṃ hūṃ | traṭ traṭ | apratihate | svāhā. Furthermore, one should spread it out with the wind-mudrā (wind-circle) and cause the space-mudrā (space-circle) to enter into its center; this is called the Universal Radiance Seal (Samantaprabhā-mudrā).
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, jvalaramale, tathāgatatrikṣe, svāhā. Furthermore, with the hands of concentration and wisdom joined in the hollow-palms gesture (*śūnyatāmudrā*), one holds the two *vāyu* wheels (index fingers) against the sides of the *tejas* wheel (middle fingers); this is called the Tathāgata-Armour Seal (*tathāgatavarmamudrā*).

"Bend the two water-wheels (anāmikā) and join the two space-wheels (tarjanī) within the palms to press upon the nails of the two water-wheels; this is the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Tongue. The mantra is:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgata-arhat-satyadharma-pratiṣṭhita svāhā*. With this seal, bend the wind- and water-wheels so they touch each other, turn the space-wheels upward and slightly bend them, join the fire-wheels (madhyamā) straight together, and do the same for the earth-wheels (aṅguṣṭha); this is named the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Gate of Speech."
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, tathāgatamahāvajratra, viśvārṇamāhodya, svāhā. As for the mudrā: using the previous seal, bend the two *vāyu-maṇḍalas* (ring fingers) into the palms with their tips pointing upward; this is called the Tathāgata-daṃṣṭrā-mudrā (the Seal of the Tathāgata’s Fangs).
The mantra is as follows:

“Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | tathāgata-ṣṭhāla | rasara-saṃkara | saṃprabhoga | sarvatathāgatānāṃ | visaya-saṃbhava | svāhā. Furthermore, with the same mudrā as before, place the two vāyu-maṇḍalas (index fingers) upward and bend their third joints; this is called the Tathāgata-pratibhāna-vyākhyāna-mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, ajitendrabhūta, rūpavāsamat-prapatta, viśuddhasvara, svāhā. Furthermore, with the hands of concentration and wisdom joined into a single form, one forms the hollow-palmed *añjali*; the two earth-wheels (*tarjanīs*) and space-wheels (*anāmikās*) are bent inward and joined together. This is the Tathāgata’s Seal of Holding the Ten Powers (*daśabala*).
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | daśamārga-dara | hūṃ saṃjñe | svāhā. Furthermore, as with the previous mudrā, join the tips of the middle joints of the two thumbs and the two index fingers; this is the Tathāgata-smṛtyupasthāna mudrā.
The mantra for that is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ tathāgatasamalatit sattvahetuparyutthita gaganasamasama svāhā. Furthermore, as with the previous mudrā, placing the two thumbs (empty wheels) upon the water-wheels is called the "Mudrā of Awakening to the Equality of All Dharmas."
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, sarvadharmasamatāprabhāsvare, tathāgatānugate, svāhā. Furthermore, join the hands of concentration and wisdom into one; place the two *vāyumaṇḍalas* (ring fingers) upon the *tejomaṇḍalas* (middle fingers), with the rest as before. This is the Samantabhadra Cintāmaṇi mudrā.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, saṃmadanugata, vīryadharmanirjāta, mahā-mahā, svāhā. Then, with the palms joined hollowly, bend the two *vāyu* fingers (the index fingers) beneath the two *tejas* fingers (the middle fingers), while the rest remain as before; this is the seal (*mudrā*) of Maitreya.
The mantra for that is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | arthajñāya | sarvasattvāśayānugata | svāhā. Furthermore, as with the previous mudrā, inserting the two space-wheels (the thumbs) into the center is called the Ākāśagarbha-mudrā.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | ākāśasamatanirgata | vicitravaradara | svāhā. Furthermore, with the same mudrā as before, bend the two water-wheels (tarjanīs) and the two earth-wheels (anāmikās) into the palms, and join the two wind-wheels (madhyamās) and the two fire-wheels (index fingers); this is the seal of Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | Āḥ sattvavajrāveśa uttiṣṭha traṃ raṃ raṃ svāhā. As before, join the hands of concentration and wisdom; extend the five fingers like small bells, and by joining and holding the thumbs and little fingers together, form the shape of a lotus. This is the seal of Avalokiteśvara.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, sarvatathāgatavajraketukarūṇamaye, ra ra ra hūṃ jaḥ svāhā. As before, form the hollow-clasp mudrā with the hands of concentration and wisdom, like an unopened lotus; this is the Mahāsthāmaprāpta seal.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, jñānajñāna svāhā. As before, with the hands of concentration and wisdom, form fists by turning the five wheels inward; extend the two wind-wheels (index fingers) like the points of needles and place the two space-wheels (thumbs) upon them—this is the mudrā of the Honored One Tārā.
The mantra for her is:

“Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, tare tvariṇi, kārūṇyopave, svāhā. As with the previous mudrā, raise the two vāyu-maṇḍalas (index fingers) and press them against each other slightly offset; this is the Vajravetālī mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | sarvabhayatrāsaṇi | hūṃ sphoṭaya | svāhā. As before, with the hands of concentration and wisdom joined in the hollow-palms gesture (*śūnyagarbha-muṣṭi*), the water-wheel and space-wheel are both inserted within; this is the seal (*mudrā*) of Sitātapatrā.
The mantra for that is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, tathāgatavisaya-sambhava padma-maṇḍini svāhā. As for the seal: as before, bend the two vāyu-cakras (index fingers) and place them beneath the ākāśa-cakra (thumbs), keeping them at a distance like a grain of barley; this is the Hayagrīva seal.
The mantra for him is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | khādaya pāñca sphoṭaya | svāhā. Using the same mudrā as before, extend the two water-wheels (ring fingers) and the two wind-wheels (little fingers), while the remaining fingers are held in a fist; this is the mudrā of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

The mantra for this is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, ha ha ha, sustaṃnu, svāhā. Furthermore, with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, form the *ākāśa-puṭa* (space-clasp) mudrā. Interlace and hold the fire-wheels (*tejas-maṇḍala*) and water-wheels (*toya-maṇḍala*), and place the two wind-wheels (*vāyu-maṇḍala*) upon the two space-wheels (*ākāśa-maṇḍala*) so that they form the shape of a hook. The remaining [details] are as before; this is the seal (*mudrā*) of the noble Mañjuśrī.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | He he kumāra | Vimuñca pātāsthititaḥ | Samara samara | Pratīrya | Svāhā. Form a fist with the *samaya*-hand, and extend the wind-wheel (the index finger) in the shape of a hook; this is the *Jālinīprabhā-aṅkuśa-mudrā*.
The mantra is as follows:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | He he kumāra | māyāgata svabhāvaviśuddha-tā | Svāhā. Then, using the same mudrā as before, slightly bend all the wheel-signs; this is the Vimalaprabhā-mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | khe-kumāra | vicitrārthakumāra | manusrāmara | svāhā. As before, form a fist with the wisdom hand; join the wind and fire wheels (the ring and middle fingers) together and extend them. This is the Khecarī-khaḍga mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | He he kumāri ke | Naye rañjanasamara | Pratītya | Svāhā. As before, form a fist with the wisdom hand and extend the fire-wheel (middle finger) in the shape of a spear; this is the spear mudrā of Upakeśinī.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | Vinayārakṣaṇe | Kūmāriki | Svāhā. As before, form a fist with the *samaya*-hand and extend the water-wheel (*tarjanī*) and earth-wheel (*anāmikā*); this is the Earth-Wisdom Banner Seal (*pṛthivīprajñādhvajamudrā*).

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, he samarañjanaketo, svāhā. Form a fist with the wisdom hand (right hand), extending the wind-wheel (index finger) in the shape of a hook; this is the mudrā for summoning the youth.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | ākarṣaya svāṃ | kuru ājñāṃ | kumārajña | svāhā. As before, form fists with the hands of concentration and wisdom; extend the two *vāyu-maṇḍalas* (index fingers) and join them at the knuckles. This is the mudrā of all those who obey the command.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, āveśāyanaye svāhā. As before, form fists with the hands of concentration and wisdom, extend the fire-wheels (middle fingers), and bend their third joints; this is the Vajra Seal for Dispelling Doubt and Wonder.
The mantra for this is:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, vimaticeṭi noga svāhā. Raising the arm of *vipaśyanā* and forming the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) constitutes the seal of the Bestower of Fearlessness.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, āpeyannanane svāhā. As before, extend the wisdom-hand and raise it upward; this is the seal for eliminating the evil realms.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, abhyudgata-sattvadhātu svāhā. As before, cover the heart with the wisdom hand; this is the *Jiuhu Huiyin* (Seal of the Wisdom of Deliverance).
The mantra is as follows:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, he mahā-mahā, samara-pratīccha, svāhā. As before, form the gesture of holding a flower with the wisdom hand; this is the seal of Mahāmaitrī-janana.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ svasti-stuta-udgata svāhā. As before, place the wisdom hand (right hand) over the heart with the fire-wheel finger (middle finger) slightly bent; this is the mudrā of Karuṇāñjali.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ karuṇā-maitrī-nidhe svāhā. As before, form the *varada-mudrā* with the right hand; this is the seal for removing all feverish afflictions (*sarva-paridāha*).
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, kṣīrābdhe, varapradāya, svāhā. As before, with the wisdom hand formed in the shape of holding a cintāmaṇi jewel, this is the seal of inconceivable wisdom (*acintyaprajñāmudrā*).
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, samayasaparivāra, svāhā. As before, form fists with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, and cause the two fire-wheels (the middle fingers) to open; this is the Seal of Kṣitigarbha’s Banner.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | Hā hā hā viśvaye | Svāhā. Form a fist with the wisdom hand (right hand) and extend the three fingers; this is the Ratnasthāna-mudrā.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, he mahā-mahā svāhā. By extending the water-wheel (anāmikā) of this wisdom hand, this is the seal of the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, ratnodvave svāhā.

Form the *viparyasta-vyatyasta* (reversed and crossed) *añjali* with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā. Interlace the *ākāśa-maṇḍala* (thumb) of the Samādhi hand with the *pṛthivī-maṇḍala* (ring finger) of the Prajñā hand; the Prajñā hand acts upon the Samādhi hand in the same manner. The remaining fingers are arranged like a *vajra*. This is the *Dharanidhara-mudrā* (Earth-Holding Seal).
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, dharani-dhara svāhā. As before, one forms the shape of a five-pronged vajra trident; this is the Jewel-Seal (*ratnamudrā*) hand gesture.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ ratnāloke svāhā. Then, by joining all the wheels with this very mudrā, it is the "Mudrā of Arousing the Firm Resolve."
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, vajrasambhava svāhā. As before, form a sword with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā; this is the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Ākāśavimala.
The mantra for that is:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ gaganananda-yo-cara svāhā. As before, the wheel mudrā is the Gaganagañjā mudrā.
The mantra is: “Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, cakravāraditi svāhā. As before, the conch-seal (śaṅkha-mudrā) is the seal of Pure Wisdom (viśuddhamati).
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, dharmasvabhāva, svāhā. As before, the lotus mudrā is the mudrā of the practice of wisdom.
The mantra for this is:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, padmarājāya svāhā. As before, the blue lotus mudrā is slightly opened; this is the Seal of the Wisdom of Abiding.
The mantra for that is:

"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ raṅgūtpādaya svāhā. As before, join the two hands together, bend the water-fingers (anāmikās) so they cross and enter into the palms, hold the two fire-fingers (tarjanīs) and earth-fingers (kaniṣṭhās) upward against each other, and extend the wind-fingers (madhyamās), bending the third joints so they do not touch, like a grain of barley; this is the Vajradhara-mudrā.
The mantra for that is:

"Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa hūṃ. As for the seal: using the previous seal, bend the two thumbs (space-fingers) and the two little fingers (earth-fingers) into the palms; this is the Maṅgala seal.
The mantra for this is:

"Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ, traṭ traṭ, jvālayanti svāhā. As before, with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, cross all the fingers in reverse, interlacing them so they turn toward one's own body; by adding the Prajñā-emptiness wheel to the Samādhi-vacuity wheel, this is the Vajra-Chain Seal (Vajraśṛṅkhalā-mudrā).
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | Hūṃ bandha bandha | Mūrchaya mūrchaya | Vajra-udbhava | Sarvatrāpratihatāya | Svāhā. With this Vajra-shackle mudrā, slightly bend the space-fingers (the thumbs) so that they hold the wind-fingers (the index fingers) without touching them; this is the wrathful Candramukhī mudrā.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. As before, form fists with the hands of concentration and wisdom, and extend the two wind-wheels (index fingers) to hold one another; this is the Vajrasūcī mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | sarvadharmānirvedanī | vajrasucivaraṇi | svāhā. As before, form fists with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā and place them at the heart; this is the Vajramuṣṭi-mudrā (Vajra-fist Seal).

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ, sphoṭaya vajrasphoṭaya svāhā. Form a fist with the *samaya*-hand, raising the fingers (the wings) and opening them wide; the *jñāna*-hand also forms a fist, but extends the *vāyu-maṇḍala* (the index finger) as if in a wrathful posture, threatening the opponent. This is the seal of Aparājita.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ, nirdariṣya mahāroṣaṇa, khādaya sattvadhātūn, svāhā. Forming fists with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, holding them in the gesture of striking, this is the Abhimukha-mudrā.
The mantra is as follows:
"Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | He abhimukha mahāparacanda | Khanadaya kinnaraya tsi | Samayam anusmara | Svāhā. As before, the gesture of holding the alms-bowl is the Śākyamuni bowl seal.
The mantra is as follows:
"Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | sarvakleśaniḥsūdana | sarvadharmavaśitāprāpta | gaganasame | svāhā. This is the Śākyamuni Ūrṇā-mudrā (Crown-tuft Seal).
As above, furthermore, by placing the tips of the fingers of the wisdom hand together and resting them upon the crown of the head, this is the Seal of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Buddhas. Its mantra is:

“Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ vaṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Forming a fist with the samaya hand, extend the fire and wind wheels (middle and index fingers), and place the space wheel (thumb) over the earth and water wheels (ring and little fingers). Extend the wind and fire wheels of the wisdom hand and insert them into the palm of the samaya hand, likewise placing the space wheel over the earth and water wheels as if within a scabbard; this is the Seal of Acala.
"As before, the Vajra Wisdom Seal (*vajrajñānamudrā*) is the Trailokyavijaya Seal.

As before, join the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā into a single form; let both the Earth and Water wheels point downward, extend the two peaks of the Fire wheels so they are joined, bend the two Wind wheels and place them upon the third joint, and align the Space wheels in the shape of three eyes."
This is the Tathāgata-Śīrṣa-mudrā, the Mother of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, with the Samādhi-hand (the left hand) turned downward and extended, and the Prajñā-hand (the right hand) formed into a fist with the wind-wheel (the index finger) raised like the shape of a parasol, this is the Śvetacchatra-Tathāgata-Śīrṣa-mudrā.
"As before, the sword mudrā is the Vijayottama-uṣṇīṣa mudrā.
As before, the wheel mudrā is the Sarvārthasiddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā.
As before, the hook mudrā—forming a fist with the wisdom hand and raising the wind-wheel (index finger) while slightly bending it—is the Karmāvaraṇaviśodhana-uṣṇīṣa mudrā."
"As before, the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā is the Fire-Cluster Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā.
As before, the Lotus mudrā is the Manifestation Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā."
"As before, the conch seal (*śaṅkhamudrā*) is the seal of the Uṣṇīṣa of Immeasurable Sound (*Amitaghoṣa*).
Forming a fist with the hand of wisdom (*prajñāhasta*) and placing it between the eyebrows is the seal of the Urṇā-kośa of the Cintāmaṇi."
"As before, the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā is the Buddha-locanā mudrā.
There is a slight difference, namely the vajra-mark.
With the wisdom hand at the heart, like holding a lotus, extend the arm of *śamatha* straight out; with the five fingers spread upward and turned outward, this is the Aparājita mudrā."
"Forming fists with the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā turned inward, bend the two space-fingers upward so they resemble a mouth; this is the mudrā of the Vidyārājñī Aparājitā.
Supporting the cheek with the hand of Prajñā is the mudrā of Maheśvara."
“By making the wind and fire wheels (anāmikā and tarjanī) crooked and extending them from this same seal, it is the seal of the Devaputra Samantakusuma.
With the same seal as before, placing the space wheel (madhyamā) within the palms, it is the seal of the Devaputra Prabhāmandita.”
"With the same mudrā as before, form the gesture of holding a flower with the space-wind wheels; this is the mudrā of the Devaputra Manasvin.
With the wisdom-hand, join the space-water wheels together, and extend the wind, fire, and earth wheels outward to cover the ears; this is the mudrā of the Devaputra Samantaghoṣa."

"When the Samādhi and Prajñā hands are joined, the two space-wheels (kha-cakra) are rounded and bent; the remaining four wheels are likewise. This is called the Earth Deity Seal (*pṛthivī-devatā-mudrā*).

As before, with the Prajñā hand forming the gesture of granting fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*) and the space-wheel placed within the palm, this is the Fire Deity Invitation Seal (*agni-devatā-āvāhana-mudrā*)."

"By means of the gesture of bestowing fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*), one holds the water-wheel (*jala-cakra*) with the second finger of the space-wheel (*ākāśa-cakra*); this is the seal of all the ṛṣis.
One should employ it accordingly according to their respective order."

"As before, join the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā; place the wind-wheel (left ring finger) and earth-wheel (right little finger) within the palms, while all other fingers point upward. This is the Yama-danda mudrā."
"The wisdom hand pointing downward like a *kaṇṭha* [bell] is the bell-seal (*ghaṇṭā-mudrā*) of Yama’s consort.
Forming a fist with the samādhi hand and extending the wind and fire fingers is the seal of Rātridevī."
"From this same mudrā, bend the wind-wheel (index finger) again; this is the trident mudrā of Rudra.
From the previous mudrā, form the shape of holding a lotus; this is the mudrā of the Brahmā-vidyārājñī."
"As before, with the seal, bend the vāyu-finger (index finger) and place it upon the third joint of the back of the agni-finger (middle finger);
this is the Kāmarī-śodhinī seal. Using this same seal, place the vāyu-finger upon the ākāśa-finger (pinky); this is the Cakra-seal of Nārāyaṇī."
"Forming a fist with the samādhi hand, extend the space-wheel (the index finger) straight upward; this is the hammer mudrā of the Seven Mothers of Yama.
Holding the concentration hand upright as if grasping a kapāla is the mudrā of Cāmuṇḍā."
"As before, the khaḍga-mudrā is the sword-mudrā of Nairṛti.
As before, the cakra-mudrā is performed with the *samaya*-hand; this is the wheel-mudrā of Nārāyaṇa."
"By joining the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā with the left and right sides interlaced, this is the Mudrā of the Two Clouds, Dhanada and Nanda.
As before, extend the Samādhi hand and join the earth and space wheels; this is the Trident Mudrā of Śaṅkara."
"As before, extend the hands in the *samādhi* gesture, with the earth and space wheels held together; this is the mudrā of Śaṅkara’s consort.
By extending the three wheels straight from this very mudrā, it becomes the mudrā of Śaṅkarī."
"Forming the lotus gesture with the hands of samādhi is the seal of Brahmā.
By performing the visualization of pure whiteness, it is the seal of Candra (the Moon God).

Manifesting the palms joined with the hands of samādhi and prajñā, bending the space-wheel (index fingers) and placing them beside the water-wheel (middle fingers), this is the seal of the palanquin of Sūrya (the Sun God)."
"Join the hands of the Prajñā-samādhi-mudrā; with the earth-wheel and wind-wheel turned inward, hold the fire-wheel and water-wheel together like a bow. This is the Śūcaye Viśūcaye-mudrā."
"As before, the banner seal (*dhvaja-mudrā*) is the seal of Vāyu.

With the *samādhi* hand facing upward at the navel wheel, the *prajñā* hand holds the space and wind fingers together and moves toward the body as if performing music; this is the *piśāca* seal of Mañjughoṣa."
"As before, the noose mudrā is the mudrā of all nāgas.
As before, the mudrā of the deity Mañjughoṣa—with the wind-finger (the little finger) bent and crossed over the space-finger (the middle finger)—is the mudrā of all asuras."
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, garārogyaṃ svāhā. Forming a fist with the hands turned inward and extending the water-wheel (ring fingers), this is the Gandharva mudrā.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ viśuddhasarvaravākṣi svāhā. Then, using this same mudrā, bend the *vāyumaṇḍala* (the index finger); this is the seal of all yakṣas.
The mantra is:
“Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, yakṣiṇī svāhā. Furthermore, with this same mudrā, holding the space-wheel and earth-wheel together while extending the fire and wind [fingers], this is the Yakṣiṇī mudrā.

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | yakṣavidyādharī | svāhā. Forming a fist with the hands turned inward and extending the index fingers (the *tejaḥ-aṅguli*), this is the mudrā of all the *piśācas*.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ viśveṣāṃ svāhā. To form the mudrā of all the Viśvedevas, bend the two fire-wheels (the index fingers).

The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, bhiñci bhiñci, svāhā. As before, join the hands of concentration and wisdom, aligning the thumbs (ākāśa-mudrā) and extending them; this is the seal of all seizing planets (sarva-graha).
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ, garbhe śmaśrīye prapate, juti-maye svāhā. Furthermore, with this mudrā, crossing the space-wheel and the fire-wheel is the seal of all constellations.
The mantra is: “Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | nakṣatrarājaniye svāhā. With this same mudrā, bend the two water-wheels (ring fingers) into the palms; this is the mudrā of all the rākṣasas.
The mantra is: “Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ ra-kṣa-sadīpataye svāhā. Extending the *samaya* hand to cover the face, touch it with the *ir-hva* [finger]; this is the seal (*mudrā*) of all *ḍākinīs*.
The mantra is: "Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ hili svāhā. O Lord of Secrets!
These foremost seals of all Tathāgatas arise from the Tathāgata’s faith and understanding; they are identical to the insignia of the Bodhisattvas, and their number is immeasurable.
Furthermore, O Lord of Mysteries!
One should know that even the movements and postures of one's limbs are all secret mudrās;
one should know that the manifold speech produced by the faculty of the tongue are all mantras.
Therefore, O Lord of Mysteries!
Bodhisattvas who practice the bodhisattva path through the gateway of mantras and have already resolved upon bodhicitta should abide in the stage of the Tathāgata and draw the maṇḍala.
"If one acts otherwise, it is equivalent to slandering all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; one will transgress the samaya and certainly fall into the evil destinies.
*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Empowerment of the Buddha’s Miraculous Transformations*, Scroll Four.
*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Empowerment of the Buddha’s Miraculous Transformations*, Scroll [Four].

Fifth: Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India and the Śramaṇa Yi Xing during the Great Tang Dynasty. Chapter Ten: The Wheel of Syllables. At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana addressed the Vajradhara Lord of Secrets, saying:
"Listen attentively,
O Lord of Secrets!
There is a dharma-gate that pervades all places."
"Lord of Secrets!
If a bodhisattva abides in this gateway of syllables, all undertakings will be fully accomplished.
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām a* *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām sa* *Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ va* *Ka kha ga gha"
Cacche jaṣṭa ṭhaṭha naḍa taṭha ta naḍha.
Bhāṣma-bāyara-rāva-śa-śa-saha.

*Kṣa* (the two syllables *kṣa* are combined; these first three turns are all pronounced with the rising tone and short vowels): *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām* *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām sa* *Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ va* *ka kha ga gha ca cha ja jha ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha*
tathāgataprabhāsvaraḥ
ŚAṢA SAHA KṢA (all these are to be pronounced with a falling tone and long vowels). "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām AṂ. "Namaḥ samantabuddhānām SAṂ. "Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ BAṂ KAṂ KHAṂ GAṂ GHAṂ ṄAṂ."
Zhàn chān rǎn zhān zhēn nán zhàn dān tān nǎn dàn.

*Jva kha gha ṅa ña cha ja jha ña ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa ta tha da dha na pa pha ba bha ma ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha kṣa* *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām oṃ namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ sva namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ mo jva kha gha ṅa ña cha ja jha ña ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa ta tha da dha na pa pha ba bha ma ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha kṣa* (Note: The characters provided represent the Sanskrit consonants with their respective *varga* (class) and *svara* (vowel) variations, including the *anusvāra* and *visarga*.
The specific instructions regarding "the first turn of the original sound" (*prathamoccāraṇa*) refer to the primary pronunciation of each letter.)
Ṭa ṭo ṇo ḍo bo bho mo bhu yo ma u lo mo śo so so ho kṣo—
all these are pronounced with the first tone (rising intonation) and the entering tone (stopping sound). I e o u.
Ṛ ṝ li lī e ai haḥ au "Aṅga ña ṇa ma ṅa śa ṇa na ma"
Hyaṃ hniṃ hnaṃ hvaṃ hmaṃ hraḥ hrīḥ hrauḥ hraḥ | Hom! "Lord of Secrets!

Such is the gateway of syllables, the path of skillful means, the sequential abiding in the Way of Mantras (Mantranaya), empowered by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas, and well-understanding the dance of the bodhisattva practices of the Perfectly Enlightened Ones. This has been taught, will be taught, and is now being taught by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present."
"Lord of Secrets!
As I now survey all the buddha-fields universally, there is none in which this Dharma-door that pervades all places is not seen; among those Tathāgatas, there is none who does not proclaim it."
Therefore, Lord of Mysteries!

Bodhisattvas who wish to fully understand the bodhisattva practice through the gateway of mantras should diligently study this dharma-door that pervades all places. By adding the initial, middle, and final syllables of *ka*, *ca*, *ṭa*, *ta*, and *pa*, and by entering them through the categories of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), they will spontaneously attain the practice of the bodhicitta, achieve perfect enlightenment, and enter parinirvāṇa.

These aforementioned gateways of syllables are mutually harmonized with the Dharma-teachings of the mantras from beginning to middle to end. If a practitioner of mantras understands them in this way, they will attain mastery according to their own mind; by applying the definitive mental application to each and every one of these phrases and perceiving them through wisdom, they shall be granted the unsurpassed and most excellent phrases.
In this way, this single wheel revolves as the wheel of syllables.
Because the mantra-practitioner understands this, they constantly illumine the world and turn the wheel of Dharma like the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana.

Chapter Eleven: The Secret Maṇḍala. At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana surveyed the entire dharma-realm with the Tathāgata-eye and entered the Dharma-realm Garbha. By means of the Tathāgata-vikrīḍita-samantavyūhagarbha-samādhi, because he manifests the inexhaustible adornments of the dharma-realm, and because he delivers the realms of all sentient beings without exception through this gateway of mantra practice, thereby fulfilling his original vows.

At that time, while the Buddha was in samādhi, from the gateway of manifold sounds within this inexhaustible realm of sentient beings, he emitted voices according to their respective types—manifesting various forms and colors, diverse languages, and the thoughts of their minds—in accordance with their inherent natures, the ripening of their karma, and their enjoyment of karmic fruits, thereby preaching the Dharma and causing all sentient beings to attain joy.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, bodies of the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) emerge; having emerged, they are equal to space. Within immeasurable worlds, with a single voice and the speech of the Dharma-realm, they proclaim these verses on the arising of the Tathāgata:
“Capable of manifesting forms according to their kind, The dharma-characteristics of all phenomena— The Buddhas and the Śrāvakas, And the Pratyekabuddhas who save the world.”
The assembly of Bodhisattvas diligent and valiant, as well as the Benevolent Honored One, likewise [arise].
The world-receptacle of sentient beings is established in succession;
all phenomena such as arising and abiding are constantly produced in this manner.
"By possessing wisdom and skillful means, one is free from the doubts of those lacking insight;
because they contemplate this path, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones have taught it.

At that time, from the body of the Tathāgata Dharmadhātusambhava, clouds of manifestations of his own body pervaded the entire realm of Vairocana. In the mere instant of a thought, immeasurable Buddhas emerged from all his pores; after successively bestowing their empowerment, they returned to the palace of the Dharmadhātu.
Then, the World-Honored One Vairocana again addressed the Secret Lord Vajradhara, saying: "Secret Lord!
There are seed-syllables and emblems for the positions of the noble deities of the maṇḍala."
"You should listen attentively and reflect upon it well; I shall now expound it. Vajradhara Guhyapati said, "So be it."
“World-Honored One!
We wish and desire to hear it.
Then the Bhagavat spoke in verse:
“The mantra practitioner establishes the maṇḍala-circle within his own body:
from his feet up to his navel, he forms the great vajra-wheel;
from there up to his heart, he should contemplate the water-wheel.”
"Upon the water wheel is the fire wheel; upon the fire wheel is the wind wheel.
Next, one should visualize and uphold the earth-holding [deity], and arrange the various forms.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi ascended into the state of the equality of the dharmas of the body, speech, and mind of the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana, and for the sake of severing all doubts of future sentient beings, he recited this Great King of Mantras:

“Namo samantabuddhānām | Asambheda-dharmadhātu | Ghaṭa-ghaṭānām | Sarvathā | Āṃ khaṃ āḥ auṃ | Saṃ saḥ | Haṃ haḥ | Raṃ vaḥ | Svāhā hūṃ | Raṃ ha ra haḥ | Svāhā raṃ ha raḥ | Svāhā. When the Vajradhara Lord of Mysteries had spoken this King of Mantras, all the Tathāgatas dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions each extended their right hands and stroked the crown of the Vajradhara, praising him with the sound of “Excellent!
Excellent, O Son of the Buddha!”

You have already transcended the stages of body, speech, and mind of the World-Honored One Vairocana; for the sake of illuminating all directions and locations, and for the sake of the bodhisattvas who abide in the path of the Mantra of Equality, you have spoken this King of Mantras.

Why is this? The World-Honored One Vairocana, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, sat upon the seat of enlightenment and contemplated the twelvefold dharma-realm (dharmadhātu). Having subdued the four māras, this dharma-realm arose and flowed forth from three locations, destroying the hosts of the celestial māra armies;

subsequently, he attained the equality of the body, speech, and mind of the World-Honored One, such that the measure of his body was equal to space, and the measures of his speech and mind were likewise so.
Having attained the arising of boundless wisdom, one teaches the Dharma with mastery over all phenomena; that is to say, this king of mantras consisting of twelve phrases.
O Son of the Buddha!
"Because you have now directly realized the equality of the body, speech, and mind of the World-Honored One Vairocana, you are known by all as one who is equal to the Truly All-Knowing One.
Then he spoke in verse:
"You inquire about the All-Knowing One, The World-Honored Buddha Mahāvairocana."
I shall now expound the Dharma teachings of the most supreme mantra practice.
It was by means of this in the past that I awakened to the wondrous Bodhi and revealed all dharmas, causing all beings to reach nirvana.
"In the worlds of the ten directions at present, all Buddhas bear witness to this.
At that time, the virtuous Vajrapāṇi, filled with great joy and sustained by the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas, spoke these verses:
"This Dharma is inexhaustible; it has no intrinsic nature and no abiding place."
Having attained liberation from karma, they are equal to the Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
All the skillful means of the World-Saviors proceed according to their compassion and vows;
they awaken to the wisdom of non-arising—that all phenomena possess such a nature.

Then the Vajradhara Lord of Mysteries further spoke an udāna verse, requesting clarification from the World-Honored One Vairocana regarding the resolution of doubts concerning this Great Maṇḍala Born of the Matrix of Great Compassion, for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages.
"Having severed all doubts, the Omniscient One is free from the fever of affliction;
for the sake of sentient beings, I ask the Teacher:
What comes first in the maṇḍala?"
May the Great Muni explain:
how many types of ācāryas are there,
and how many kinds of disciples?
How does one know the characteristics of the earth?
How does one select and prepare it?
How should one purify it?
How do they abide firmly, and how do they purify their disciples?
We pray that the Guide will explain this.
What are the characteristics of those who have already been purified?
By what means is protection performed?
How is the ground consecrated?
Who initiates the ritual activity?
How many sūtras are there?
How are they divided into sections?
How many kinds of offerings are there to be cultivated?
What are these flowers and incense? To whom should these flowers be offered?
Incense is likewise so; how should it be presented? With what kind of flowers and incense should one offer them?
Regarding the various offerings and homas, by what ritual procedures are they performed?
As well as the seats of the various noble deities, I pray that you explain these teachings.
Please expound upon them in their proper sequence, revealing the physical forms and manifest colors.
Regarding the honored secret mudrās and the seats one spreads for oneself:
why are they called "mudrās," and from what do these mudrās arise?
How many kinds of consecration are there?
How many samayas are there?
For how long must the mantra-practitioner diligently cultivate the practice of mantra?
How does one become endowed with the Bodhisattva path?
How does one perceive the ultimate truth?
How many kinds of siddhi are there?
And when [the practice] is accomplished, how does one ascend into the great void?
How is the body secret, such that without abandoning this very body, one attains a celestial body?
From what do these various transformations arise?
The sun, moon, fire, and the directions; the luminaries, constellations, planets, and divisions of time;
the various ill omens that appear; and the manifold sufferings endured within birth and death—[from what do they all originate?]
How can one cause [afflictions] not to arise, so that what has arisen is completely extinguished,
and thereby attain constant proximity to the Buddhas, the Honored Ones among two-legged beings?
How many kinds of homa fires are there, and through how many matters is their majesty increased?
The distinct natures of all Buddhas, I pray that the Guide will explain.
Regarding all other worlds, as well as the supramundane,
their fruits and their quantities, and the most excellent samādhis—
In what state is one matured?
What constitutes lack of maturity?
Furthermore, after how much time does one attain liberation from birth through karma?
The Fully Awakened One, the Omniscient One, the World-Honored One free from feverish affliction,
addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"The secret maṇḍala is the definitive station of the noble deities."
The source of great compassion, the unsurpassed Mahāyāna,
the supreme secret of all Buddhas— just as you have asked,
O Great Powerful Vajra-holder, I shall now briefly proclaim it.
Regarding the initial practice of the maṇḍala, the sons of the Buddha should listen attentively.
The twelve-syllable mantra, which gives birth to the powerful Vidyārāja,
is that which must be performed first of all.
Abiding in this fundamental samādhi, one understands the path of yoga and performs all manner of activities.
There are two kinds of ācāryas: those who have mastered mudrās and mantras;
their characteristics are likewise twofold, consisting of the profound-secret and the manifest-abridged divisions.
One who can understand the profound and vast meaning should only transmit it to those worthy of receiving it;
such a true son of the Perfectly Awakened One remains far removed from worldly pleasures.
The second type seeks the phenomena of the present life, being deeply attached to ignorance and its objects of perception.
The worldly maṇḍalas are all created for this purpose. The Buddhas,
the Honored Ones among bipeds, and the masters who transmit the empowerment and teachings,
speak of four kinds of disciples, distinguished by whether the time is appropriate or inappropriate.
First is recitation at the proper time, non-time, both, or neither;
possessing all these characteristics, the Buddha calls one a true disciple.
From the very beginning, knowing the signs of the stages is what is called the "mind-ground."
I have already explained the purification, as practiced in one's former activities.
If one is free from faults and afflictions, and the mind-ground is without fear,
one shall attain true purity and be liberated from all transgressions.
Firmly abiding in such knowledge, one perceives one’s own *sambodhi*;
if it were otherwise than this, it would not be the ground of purification.
If one dwells in false conceptualization, the practitioner purifies that ground.
"Lord of Secrets, it is not pure because it is devoid of the bodhicitta;
therefore, one should abandon conceptualization and purify all stages.
I have extensively taught the dharma-instructions for all maṇḍalas."
Regarding the primary matters herein, the ignorant do not know or understand them;
this is not called worldly awakening, nor is it omniscience,
for they are unable even to relinquish the conceptualization of the causes of all suffering.
One should purify the bodhicitta for the disciple, protecting them with Acala or Trailokyavijaya.
If the disciple does not do so, they will be moved by false attachments.
One shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment, stainless like space.
The first empowerment is this ground, relying upon the teachings of all Buddhas;
the second is mastery of mind, which exists only here and not in other teachings.
There are four kinds of *sūtra*—namely white, yellow, red, and black;
the fifth to be contemplated is the color of space. By performing meditative concentration (*samādhi*) within that space, one seals and establishes the maṇḍala.
Second, take the thread and place it upon the site of the maṇḍala;
it is the seat of all Tathāgatas and of the sons of the Buddhas’ wisdom—
delightful and wondrous lotuses, which the world calls auspicious.
The Pratyekabuddhas and the Śrāvakas— those known as those with limited wisdom—
should know that the seats spread for them are lotus leaves and blue lotus petals;
as for the various devas of the world, headed by the Brahmakāyika gods, [their seats are likewise prepared].
The red padma flower is called the King of Seats;
descending here as is appropriate, one should mindfully dwell upon its location.
There are four kinds of offerings: namely, prostration and joining the palms.
Together with compassion and the rest,
flowers arise from the hands; offering them to the Protectors of the World,
one forms the mudrās born of the limbs and contemplates the bodhicitta.
Each and every Tathāgata and those born from them,
with these faultless flowers— fragrant, exquisite, and radiant—
take the Dharma-realm as the king of trees to make offerings to the Honored One among Sages.
Through the empowerment of truthful speech, the sovereign turning of samādhi,
and clouds of supreme, wondrous, and vast [qualities], they arise within the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
From them, a rain of various flowers falls, constantly pervading before all Buddhas.
The other world-protectors and deities likewise should scatter these flowers;
they should be offered according to what is appropriate for each.
For the nature of the original mantras and their classes, the same applies accordingly to the unguents and so forth.
The space and water wheels support one another; this is called the Auspicious Seal (Śrīvatsa-mudrā).
Whatever flowers and other offerings he receives, one should present them from one's own heart.
As for the various worldly deities, one should know that they reside at the position of the navel.
Or with the mudrā of the vajra-fist, or again with a lotus garland,
one should offer them in the air to the Teacher, the Savior of the World,
and likewise to all the world-protectors, each according to their proper order.
Homa is of two kinds, namely internal and external.
That which brings liberation from the karma produced by actions, and further gives rise to the sprout of [awakening],
is called internal homa because it is able to incinerate karma.
The external application has three stages; dwelling within these three stages, one accomplishes the paths of the three karmas—this is the supreme worldly homa.
If one acts otherwise than this, they do not understand the rite of homa.
That deluded one fails to obtain the fruit, having abandoned the wisdom of mantra.
One should know that the mantras of the Tathāgata family and those spoken by all the Perfectly Enlightened Ones are white and yellow; the Vajra [family] possesses all colors.
The mantra of Avalokiteśvara is purely white, shifting according to the specific rite;
its four sides are layered and universal, and the circular wheel follows the proper sequence.
The three corners and the half-moon wheel—their forms are likewise described as such.
First, one should know that forms and images— namely, the bodies of men and women,
or those in all places— arise according to their respective classes,
colors, and shapes through inconceivable wisdom; therefore, it is inconceivable.
